feed_title: Mushroom murderer Erin Patterson launches last-ditch High Court appeal
title: Erin Patterson: Mushroom murderer launches last-ditch High Court appeal
content_text:
Mushroom murderer Erin Patterson launches last-ditch High Court appeal
- Published
Australia's mushroom killer Erin Patterson has launched a final legal bid to overturn her murder convictions and avoid dying in jail.
Erin Patterson, 52, was last year found guilty of murdering three relatives and attempting to kill another when she served them a toxic mushroom-laced meal in 2023.
Last month, in Victoria's Court of Appeal three judges dismissed an appeal against her convictions and threw out the possibility she could be released on parole – saying her crimes were "extraordinarily cold and calculated" and had to be "denounced in the strongest terms".
She has now made a last-ditch application to the High Court to look at her case.
Patterson had 28 days to file an application for special leave to appeal to the High Court, a deadline which expired on Friday.
She wants the country's top judges to examine both her conviction and sentence - but the court does not have to agree to look at the case. It only hears appeals in about 10% of cases.
After a high-profile trial last year, a jury found Patterson guilty of murdering her in-laws, Don and Gail Patterson, and Gail's sister Heather Wilkinson, by serving them individual portions of beef Wellington containing death cap mushrooms which she had tracked down, foraged and prepared.
Patterson was also found guilty of the attempted murder of Heather's husband Ian Wilkinson, a local pastor, who also ate the toxic lunch at Patterson's home in rural Victoria.
He survived after spending weeks in hospital and has ongoing health issues due to the poisoning.
Simon Patterson, the host's estranged husband, was meant to attend the lunch but cancelled at the last minute, in part due to his belief that his wife had repeatedly tried to poison him over several years.
Patterson was sentenced last September, with the trial judge allowing a non-parole period of 33 years due to the "harsh prison conditions" she would likely face. This glimmer of hope of freedom was thrown out by the appeal judges, who ruled she should never be released.
She had argued her conviction was unsafe on seven grounds - including a hotel booking mix up which saw the jury stay in the same place as the prosecution, a key police witness and the media.
Her lawyers said this was "catastrophic" and undermined the integrity of her trial, but the appeal court judges dismissed all the grounds for appeal.

clean_title: Venezuela to scrap law that bars opposition from public office
feed_title: Venezuela to scrap law that bars opposition from public office
title: Venezuela to scrap law that bars opposition from public office
content_text:
Venezuela to scrap law that bars opposition from public office
- Published
Venezuela will repeal a law that bars opposition figures from assuming public office, the speaker of the National Assembly Jorge Rodríguez has said.
The legislation, which was introduced two years ago, has been criticised for enabling political persecution, but Rodríguez said no politician had been subjected to its provisions.
The older brother of Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodríguez said he expected the reforms to be approved next week.
Delcy Rodríguez's interim government has been negotiating with opposition parties since taking over at the start of the year, when former President Nicolás Maduro was seized by the United States.
The legislation, known as the Simón Bolívar Law, was passed shortly after the election in July 2024 in which then-incumbent Maduro was declared the winner amid widespread allegations of fraud.
Under the legislation, individuals who requested or supported foreign sanctions against Venezuela were permanently banned from political office and had their assets confiscated.
"Legislative processes are dynamic processes. That law responded to a very specific moment in a particular situation that Venezuela was going through," Jorge Rodríguez said.
During subsequent talks, which began in August, the interim government and parts of the opposition agreed to review several other laws as part of a "route map towards democracy", according to an opposition statement.
Delcy Rodríguez has promised that the South American country will hold free and fair elections, without setting a date.
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado is widely expected to run for office in the event of an election despite being excluded from transition talks.
Machado returned to the country in October after more than 10 months in exile.
In the 2024 election, Machado's ally Edmundo González ran in her place after she was barred from running for office by Maduro's government.
The electoral authority, which was closely aligned with the government, declared Maduro the winner without making detailed voting tallies public.
The opposition argued that González won the election, not Maduro, uploading copies of the voting tallies as evidence.

clean_title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo's Lubero town amid diplomatic row
feed_title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row
title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo's Lubero town amid diplomatic row
content_text:
Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row
- Published
Uganda has announced plans to withdraw its troops from a town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo within two weeks, as diplomatic tensions escalate between the two neighbours.
The troops will hand over security in Lubero, in North Kivu province, to Congolese forces after nearly two years of military operations, the Ugandan army said in a statement on Friday.
The announcement comes days after DR Congo summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over controversial social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is the son of President Yoweri Museveni.
The Ugandan military did not give a reason for the withdrawal or say whether it was linked to the diplomatic row.
The Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) were deployed to Lubero to pursue fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) Islamist group fleeing joint military operations elsewhere in eastern DR Congo.
The ADF, which originated in Uganda in the 1990s, is affiliated to the Islamic State and has been blamed for numerous deadly attacks on civilians in both countries.
Uganda first deployed troops to eastern DR Congo under the current joint military campaign in November 2021, following a series of bomb attacks in the Ugandan capital, Kampala.
Ugandan army spokesperson Col Chris Magezi said that the joint military campaign, known as Operation Shujaa, would continue elsewhere in DR Congo.
The planned withdrawal applies only to Lubero town.
Five years into the joint offensive, the ADF remains DR Congo's deadliest armed group, despite a significant decline in its activities in Uganda, according to the conflict monitoring organisation Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (Acled).
John Ngono, Acled's DR Congo analyst, said the group was killing an average of four civilians a day and had expanded into previously unaffected parts of eastern DR Congo.
He said the findings suggested that "Operation Shujaa may have improved security in Uganda while shifting the geographical impact of violence within the DRC".
Acled says the group has not carried out an attack in Uganda since June 2025, but its growing interest in mineral resources in DR Congo could help finance its operations and sustain its ability to threaten both countries.
The planned withdrawal comes amid strained relations between Uganda and DR Congo, despite years of close military co-operation.
Earlier this week, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to endorse a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo, threatening that Ugandan troops would seize it themselves if the rebels failed to do so.
The Congolese foreign ministry described his remarks as "particularly serious" and demanded that Uganda clarify its official position and take steps to prevent similar incidents.
Gen Kainerugaba also defended Uganda's military presence in eastern DR Congo, insisting it was driven by security concerns.
The planned withdrawal comes amid renewed fighting between Congolese forces and rebels in the wider Lubero territory, raising fresh concerns about the safety of civilians.
Eastern DR Congo has endured decades of conflict involving dozens of armed groups, with millions of people forced to flee their homes.

clean_title: Noida: 164 foreigners rescued from cyberfraud racket
feed_title: India busts cyberfraud and trafficking network rescuing 164 foreigners
title: Noida: 164 foreigners rescued from cyberfraud racket
content_text:
India busts cyberfraud and trafficking network rescuing 164 foreigners
- Published
Police in India say they have uncovered an international cyberfraud and human trafficking operation on the outskirts of capital city Delhi and rescued 92 Indonesian and 72 Malaysian nationals.
They were allegedly lured to India with promises of lucrative IT jobs, but forced into cyber crime, according to police.
Police say the scheme was exposed after a Malaysian worker managed to escape and revealed the operation.
Dozens of foreign nationals have alleged that once they arrived in India, their passports were confiscated and they were held against their will in Noida - a Delhi suburb that is a major IT and business hub in northern India and home to several call centres.
Instead of the jobs and high salaries promised, police say, they were forced to pose as women online to lure unsuspecting victims into fake investment platforms.
So far one Malaysian national has been arrested in connection with the crime, and nearly 550 desktop computers, laptops and mobile phones have been confiscated, police say.
An investigation has now been launched into a potential wider global cyberfraud network.
Police and Indian banks have been trying to contend with an alarming rise in cyber fraud operations in recent years.
A paper, external by the Reserve Bank of India warned against rising digital fraud and "the manipulation of users through social engineering, coercion, or impersonation".
Figures from India's National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal show 2.8 million cyber fraud complaints were recorded in 2025, with losses of about 22,495 crore rupees, external ($2.42bn; £1.85 bn). It's a dramatic rise in complaints by more than 4,000% since 2021.
The federal government said most cases involved fake investment and trading scams.
In fake investment scams, fraudsters approach victims through social media, messaging groups or phone calls, posing as financial experts and promising high returns.
They lure victims to fake trading platforms that show fictitious profits. Some are allowed to withdraw small amounts to build trust, but when they try to cash out larger sums, they are blocked or asked to pay more. The fraudsters eventually disappear with their money.
The Noida case is the latest in a series of international cyberfraud call centres busted in north India in recent months, with police raids in Lucknow and Delhi's Pitampura area.
In July, Lucknow Police arrested 119 people after raiding a fake international call centre targeting US citizens. Employees allegedly posed as representatives of major companies and US government agencies to defraud victims.

clean_title: EU leaders fail to bridge budget splits as talks stall
feed_title: EU leaders fail to bridge budget splits as talks stall
title: EU leaders fail to bridge budget splits as talks stall
content_text:
EU leaders fail to bridge budget splits as talks stall
- Published
European Union (EU) leaders have deferred negotiations on its long-term budget after tensions surfaced over the bloc's spending priorities and aid for Ukraine.
Tense talks on the 2028-34 budget ended after 12 hours on Thursday at a summit in Brussels, with some members walking out of negotiations that will resume in December.
Divisions were largely split along the lines of countries, including France and Italy, wanting to approve a higher-spending proposal against those advocating for financial restraint, with Germany chief among them.
Many members want the budget locked in ahead of several high-stakes elections held across Europe in 2027, including in France.
Countries remain divided over a proposal to provide Ukraine with an additional loan of €45bn (£37.6bn), split between non-military and military funding.
Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Hungary have objected to the loan, but German Chancellor Frederich Merz said uniform EU agreement was a condition for approving the broader budget.
"I stand by my view that aid for Ukraine must be supported by the European Union as a whole," Merz told reporters.
"The European Union comprises of 27 member states, not 23 or 24."
Bulgaria, which previously opposed the plan, said it would agree to fund part of the loan that commits non-military financial support to Kyiv, marking a small sign of progress emerging from the special summit of the European Council.
EU members have been wrangling over the long-term budget after the European Commission submitted a €2tn proposal earlier this year, with some countries objecting to high levels of spending.
Those advocating higher spending want the funds to future-proof industries such as farming and invest in regional development. Fiscally cautious countries want to avoid amassing ballooning debt.
Thursday's talks were set up by the European Council to unblock the impasse, with a proposal to reduce spending by approximately €220bn to €230bn.
Under the current proposal, the budget totals €1.582tn, which includes €140bn to repay pandemic-era borrowing.
Four countries wanting to rein in the budget, including Denmark and Austria, walked out of negotiations after several hours of meetings.
Merz said there was "new movement" towards reducing the size of the EU budget, though he added "we are not there yet" when he confirmed that a new round of negotiations would not take place in Brussels on Friday.
European budgets requires approval from all 27 countries, with each country effectively holding veto power.
French President Emmanuel Macron said it would be a "strategic mistake" to lower long-term spending.
France's forthcoming presidential election came into focus during the EU budget talks, with frontrunner Marine Le Pen calling the talks an "underhanded political manoeuvring to thwart the democratic will of the French people".
Last month, Le Pen announced she would significantly reduce French aid to Ukraine and EU contributions if she were to win the presidency.
Macron addressed Le Pen's remarks on the sidelines of the Brussels summit, saying: "It is an odd kind of arrogance to behave as if she is already in charge of France's destiny because, as things stand, she has not been elected."
Once the talks concluded, the European Council announced a two-day summit on 17 and 18 December would revive budget negotiations.
Spanish economist Pablo Hernández de Cos was also named as the next President of the European Central Bank, replacing Christine Lagarde from February 2027.

clean_title: New Zealand election results: Ruling coalition loses parliamentary majority
feed_title: New Zealand's ruling coalition falls short of parliamentary majority by one seat
title: New Zealand election results: Ruling coalition loses parliamentary majority
content_text:
New Zealand's ruling coalition falls short of parliamentary majority by one seat
- Published
New Zealand's ruling coalition has fallen short of a parliamentary majority by one seat, following a campaign shaped by a sluggish economy and disillusioned voters.
It now needs the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to remain in power. If they cannot reach a deal, the country may have to go back to the polls.
The incumbent National Party led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon secured 40 out of 130 seats, while its coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First took 13 and 12 respectively.
A government led by the centre-left Labour Party is not possible, official results on Friday show, as the bloc would not have enough seats even if Opportunity threw its weight behind it.
Luxon on Friday acknowledged that negotiations "may be challenging" and will take some time.
"Kiwis won't thank us for rushing to an agreement that falls apart or for sending them back to the polls," he told reporters.
Labour leader Chris Hipkins said his party "ran an incredible campaign" but acknowledged that it doesn't have negotiating power despite winning the popular vote. "More New Zealanders voted for change at this election than for the status quo," he said.
New Zealand's mixed-member proportional voting system means most governments are coalitions. Each person casts two votes – one for their preferred political party and another for their choice of local representative.
Labour secured 36 seats, The Greens took 17, while Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests, picked up five.
Opportunity, which has been described as this election's kingmaker, secured seven seats. Opportunity's leader Qiulae Wong told reporters her party will negotiate with National, but that all options remain on the table.
"There are seven parties in parliment and everyone is responsible for making sure we do everything we can to deliver a stable government for New Zealand. It's not just up to us," she said on Friday.
Preliminary results on 7 November, election day, had projected that National combined with its coalition partners would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc.
But today's official tally shows it had lost two seats on special votes - cast by citizens who were overseas or outside of their registered electorate on election day - which typically skew left.
Some of National's key election pledges include lower taxes, cheaper energy, more renewable generation, and a greater focus on defence.
Labour, meanwhile, had campaigned to cut healthcare, public transport and fuel costs, more government support for social housing, among other things.
In earlier interviews with the BBC, many voters had expressed frustration over spiralling costs of living and high unemployment across the country, with declining faith in their political leadership.
"There's this kind of apathy and a bit of dread," said 21-year-old Imogen Vlutger.
A 40-year-old man said he didn't vote as he could not bring himself to tick any of the boxes on the ballot paper.
More than half of the country no longer see New Zealand as a land of opportunity, according to a survey by the Helen Clark Foundation, a public policy think tank.
Kiwis have been leaving the country in record numbers, with many of them, including former prime minister Jacinda Arden, moving to Australia.

clean_title: European games marred by clashes as French President Emmanuel Macron condemns violence
feed_title: Clashes mar European games as Macron condemns violence
title: European games marred by clashes as French President Emmanuel Macron condemns violence
content_text:
Clashes mar European games as Macron condemns violence
- Published
Violent clashes marred a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French president Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.
There were also incidents at games between Turkish side Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia and Sunderland's 1-1 home draw with Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok.
In Marseille, the build-up to the Europa League match at the Stade Velodrome was affected by incidents in the stands, including the throwing of projectiles and flares between the two sets of supporters.
With 10 minutes to go until kick-off, several Marseille fans ran from a home stand, appearing to pursue a group of Levski Sofia supporters.
They breached the stand designated for away fans, which housed around 500 supporters of the Bulgarian domestic champions.
"Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," said the Marseille police prefecture. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds."
Macron spoke to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev about the incidents, with the French president condemning "with the utmost force these acts of violence, which have no place in sport or in public space", and reassured him that "these acts would not go unpunished".
According to news agency Reuters, Radev thanked Macron for his personal involvement following the "attack on Bulgarian citizens" and for the medical assistance provided to the victims.
Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said she found video footage of the incidents "shocking" in a statement posted on social media.
"The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she added.
"Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety."
Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents".
The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests".
Security personnel managed to restore calm, allowing the game to kick-off on time, although there were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break in a match Marseille won 1-0.
"It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez
Marseille boss Bruno Genesio added: "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable."
Meanwhile, the Turkish Football Federation has strongly condemned the "unacceptable" actions of Georgian police towards Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during their Europa League match against Israeli side Hapoel Be'er-Sheva.
Besiktas say they have lodged a complaint with European football's governing body Uefa over "disproportionate" use of force by Georgian police.
The match had been moved from Istanbul to Batumi, Georgia for safety and security reasons but had to be suspended in the 25th minute after clashes involving Besiktas supporters and local police.
Both the officiating team and the Besiktas players left the field, but play was able to resume 30 minutes later.
Besiktas won the match 2-1.
"We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the Uefa Europa League match," said a statement from the Turkish federation.
Turkish outlet NTV reported that Georgian police had gone into the stands and used pepper spray on the Besiktas fans.
The report added that there were anti-Israeli chants from the Turkish fans and that Besiktas players and director of football Onder Ozen spoke to supporters to try to calm matters before play restarted.
Hakan Fidan, Turkey's minister of foreign affairs, spoke to his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili following the incident.
"All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights," a Turkish foreign ministry source said.
At Sunderland, there were crowd disturbances after Jagiellonia Bialystok fans were found in areas of the Stadium of Light with home fans, despite Uefa having imposed an away supporter ban for the Europa League game.
Police and stewards attended some disruption early on during the match.
"In the build-up to the match, the club had put measures in place in line with this sanction and maintained regular communication with our supporters, Jagiellonia Bialystok and Uefa," said a Sunderland statement.
"Unfortunately, Jagiellonia Bialystok failed to engage and cooperate on this matter.
"We are disappointed that these measures and communications were disregarded by some visiting supporters and we will review the circumstances surrounding their entry into the stadium."

clean_title: "Does changing where games run cross a legal line?" Microsoft-owned Github ask in now-deleted post celebrating GTA 6's effect on PC port-focused PS5 emulator
feed_title: "Does changing where games run cross a legal line?" Microsoft-owned Github ask in now-deleted post celebrating GTA 6's effect on PC port-focused PS5 emulator
title: "Does changing where games run cross a legal line?" Microsoft-owned Github ask in now-deleted post celebrating GTA 6's effect on PC port-focused PS5 emulator
content_text:
"Does changing where games run cross a legal line?" Microsoft-owned Github ask in now-deleted post celebrating GTA 6's effect on PC port-focused PS5 emulator
"GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on GitHub"
'Yay, GTA 6 is out on consoles and lots of people are playing it' is a fairly harmless thing to say. Unless you're, I dunno, a development platform mentioning that in a post celebrating the recent success of a PS5 emulator used for making unofficial PC ports of console games. You know, the sorts of unofficial PC ports vibecoders and proper coders having been scrambling to make of GTA 6 since its Xbox executable was allegedly leaked. The sorts of unofficial PC ports publishers like Rockstar tend to quickly move to have taken down.
"GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on Github," read a Github tweet screengabbed by Kotaku before it was deep sixed. "The repo AnyPS5 has passed 58K stars since its August launch, rewriting PS5 executables to run on Windows and Linux. Does changing where games run cross a legal line? Share your take. Happy GTA VImas!"
A video alongside the post seems to have dug the hole even deeper. "The project rewrites a game's executable so Windows and Linux can run it directly," a presenter cheerily declared. "Performance seems to be the main issue for users wanting to run GTA 6, with one contributor telling the project's community to lock in and get their agents to help if they need to." From there, the "big question" of whether it's actually legal to change where and how your games run was posed by Github.
And now their tweet is deleted. Here was the text. https://t.co/kNbmmPCGdf
— Cisc0 (@PikminGuts92) November 26, 2026
One can only imagine how raised the eyebrows of Rockstar affiliated lawyers may have become if they read the post before Github yanked it.
Another big question posed a lot recently is whether the threat of bodged PC recreations based on the alleged leaked executable may lead Rockstar to narrow the gap between GTA 6's console release and its eventual Windows launch, which reports have previously claimed is planned for the opening months of next year. You know, because the company and publishers Take-Two presumably don't want to risk the sales of an official port being undercut by an unofficial one, no matter the degree of impact that might actually have (my presumption would be the official port would still rake in a fortune).
Given the reception their baffling AnyPS5 post received, I doubt Github'll be providing any more commentary on the rush to unofficially port GTA 6 and the debate as to when it might hit PC officially.

title: Are you a warlock tired of being summon-kicked in World of Warcraft: Forever? There's now a mod to fight back with
content_text:
Are you a warlock tired of being summon-kicked in World of Warcraft: Forever? There's now a mod to fight back with
Fel-weather friends.
Being recruited to a World of Warcraft party as a warlock, only to be swiftly kicked again after using your powers to magically summon the party members together in the same place, may soon become a thing of the past. All thanks to a mod made by one especially peeved warlock.
The practice of exploiting warlocks in this way is called summon-kicking, and aside from the in-game reporting feature, there is little recourse to admonish such behavior.
Enter Summoners Union, the add-on mod, which grants the ability to flag and track players who summon-kick thereby building a collective case against them.
The mod was showcased on the World of Warcraft: Forever Reddit by user 274Moons, highlighting its ability to flag players after they boot you from a party, but also that it warns you if anyone in the party has a record of summon-kicking. It can also be combined with an in-game chat channel where warlock comrades can pull together and discuss and ultimately maybe fend off this nasty behavior.
"I play a lock and got tired of the usual 'hey can you summon?', ten minutes at the stone, last person comes through, *You have been removed from the group.*," 274Moons wrote. "So I made an addon about it. It's called The Summoners Union."
According to the add-on's creator, over 500 Warlocks have already downloaded Summon Union. It's a relatively small number in comparison to the wider World of Warcraft: Forever population, but it's a notable start.
"Thank you for this, I hate being just a taxi," wrote user Gregore997. Others also were quick to thank 274Moons for their service to all the Warlocks out there, such as Nangz who wrote: "Please keep the community sharing!".
World of Warcraft: Forever has been out for a little while now and it's been received rather well, breaking records for the series in terms of active players. The playerbase is currently awaiting the release of the game's first raids next month.

clean_title: Rockstar boss "so grateful" to have kept GTA 6's big prologue twist a secret - and reveals Tomás' story was almost very different
feed_title: Rockstar boss "so grateful" to have kept GTA 6's big prologue twist a secret - and reveals Tomás' story could have been very different
title: Rockstar boss "so grateful" to have kept GTA 6's big prologue twist a secret - and reveals Tomás' story was almost very different
content_text:
Rockstar boss "so grateful" to have kept GTA 6's big prologue twist a secret - and reveals Tomás' story could have been very different
"Multiple times throughout development, people were like, 'Can it not be...'"
If you've played the first 20 minutes or so of Grand Theft Auto 6, you'll know there's a hugely significant plot revelation there - one Rockstar somehow managed to keep entirely secret until the game's launch.
It's somewhat miraculous they did, given the many leaks the studio has suffered until now. And while, frankly, the embargo restrictions around discussing it in our GTA 6 review made a deeper analysis of Jason and Lucia's story more than a little awkward, I'm also mostly glad it remained a surprise. It's one of the great twists delivered in a game of this kind.
Speaking to Eurogamer in an interview shortly before GTA 6 was released, Rockstar Games' head of development Rob Nelson discussed the secret and, notably, the fact the team also discussed going another way entirely.
Spoilers for GTA 6's opening half hour - and further backstory around that moment from later in the game - below.
The big twist of course is that Jason and Lucia have a young child, Tomás, who we see Lucia abandoning in order to rob a store at gunpoint during the game's prologue.
It's an astonishing moment, both in the complexity it immediately lends Lucia, who is at once painted in a more negative light as a result, and in the stakes it affords her and Jason. This is the first time GTA's protagonists have genuine, human stakes that underpin their actions during the game's story, and at the same time Rockstar, in doing so, opens a route for itself to offering a far more nuanced take on modern crime.
But it was also something of a risk – and a hotly debated one, as Nelson told me during our conversation – as giving the game's protagonists that kind of narrative weight ran somewhat counter to the crime movie, straight-to-the-action thrills of previous GTAs.
"I'm so grateful that we managed to keep that under wraps," Nelson said. The subversion of expectations was intentional. "You feel like you maybe know these characters, or what the game or the story is going to be about, and then in the first 10, 15 minutes, it takes on a completely different context."It was an idea that came about organically. "But the idea of the character wanting something that maybe is at odds with what you thought you wanted as a player coming in, which is amassing as much material wealth as possible, and as many cars, and as many things," he said, was something Rockstar found particularly compelling.
The next point of the studio's focus then became the justification for Lucia's decision, Nelson explained. "The story was always, broadly, going to go through some of the major beats that it did," once Rockstar decided on the key points of the protagonists being a couple and them having a child. "But the details of the relationship, the narrative details of it, we dialled in a lot - because we're doing a lot there. She's leaving a kid early on – that's not a very sympathetic move to make."
That led to the decision to show, later in the story, more about why Lucia opted to leave Tomás in that moment. "Many chapters later, where [Jason] is like: 'What? Why did you do that?' And she has a flashback to sort of being at her wit's end," Nelson said, which then flows into the question of why she left Jason in the first place. "Cal asks Jason, 'Why did she leave?' And so, well, she didn't know she was pregnant at the time. 'Okay, but why didn't she call you?' 'Well, because I might've told her I didn't want [to be a father].' So you have to just make sure that you can understand both of their perspectives."
The tension from the fact they had a child, and that the two of them were away from their son as you play the game, was significant enough to become a point of discussion within the studio.
"Multiple times throughout development, we had this child, and people are like, 'Can it not be, like, theirs?'" Nelson said. "'Could it be like her little sister? Could it be– because I really feel bad having a good time in Vice City…' and the questions are valid," he continued. "But it wouldn't be powerful if not. So it was up to us to figure out how [you resolve that tension]."
Like with Lucia's justification for leaving Tomás - revealed in a striking dream-slash-flashback later in the game, that mixes typically exaggerated Rockstar satire with genuine social commentary - this then led to a cascade of other character moments. "How about he's in a better position than he would ever be with them, and so he's with her aunt, who's way more stable, and has a loving husband and other little kids, and he's always having a good time?" Nelson said.
He points to a conversation between Jason and Lucia in the game's first chapter as another example. "Very early on, in chapter one, they have this chat where he's like, 'Let's FaceTime - FruitFace is the thing we use - and she's like, 'No, I don't want to confuse him. He's better off until we get our shit together.' And he's like 'Okay' and she's like, 'It's not a cop-out', and he's like, 'No, no, I met my father on the other side of a glass divider, so I'm kind of trying to break that cycle.' And that's right in chapter one, and so it's a thread all the way through."
The result, then, is that the decision to add Tomás ultimately shaped many of the key parts of Jason and Lucia's characters, from their relationships with their own parents – Jason's being in jail, and Lucia's mother too narcissistic to help – to what is, really, the entire narrative arc of the story. And rightly so; a child is a big deal, and one of many reasons why GTA 6 is able to tap into something deeper than any of the previous games in the series before.
We've much more from our interview with Rob Nelson to come over the following days. In the meantime, he discussed why Rockstar made a form of honour system a core part of GTA 6's design (spoiler: because thinking more deeply about your in-game choices is fun). And in other Rockstar news, the studio has surprised those keeping up with its ongoing unionisation efforts by voting against formal recognition of the Rockstar Game Workers' Union.
PS5, Xbox Series X/S

clean_title: Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences
feed_title: Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences
title: Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences
content_text:
The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now. Or else.
Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”
Shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”
Days later, the board gave the administration what it wanted. “It is my Great Honor to report that the United States of America now fully owns and controls 10% of INTEL,” Donald Trump posted to his social platform. “The United States paid nothing for these Shares, and the Shares are now valued at approximately $11 Billion Dollars. This is a great Deal for America.”
President Trump was similarly jubilant on Monday, announcing that he had “convinced” Nvidia’s board of directors to rehire chief executive Jensen Huang. The proclamation was a shock. But it wasn’t entirely without precedent.
Fifteen months earlier, the Trump administration had interfered with the leadership decisions at another major chipmaker, court documents allege. Then, as now, allegations swirled that the company’s CEO was too close to China. Then, as now, the Trump administration dealt itself into the company’s financial future.
It’s part of a broader shift within the government in general and the Commerce Department in particular, a former member of that department tells WIRED. Out are old metrics “like creating jobs or the US being more competitive or owning more of the market share,” this ex-Trump administration official says. When dealing with private companies, a single overriding concern is: “Are you going to give back to the government in cash?”

clean_title: Pizza history: AI agent’s cardless purchase is a first for UK
feed_title: Pizza history: AI agent's cardless purchase is a first for UK
title: Pizza history: AI agent’s cardless purchase is a first for UK
content_text:
An order of Papa John’s margherita pizzas has become the first purchase in the UK to be made using an AI agent using cardless payment technology.
The order of nine mini pizzas was made as part of the Financial Conduct Authority’s (FCA) regulated sandbox trials to test the technology, using Lloyds Bank and payment specialist TrueLayer.
London-based TrueLayer, which enables payments to be made between bank accounts without using cards, said it was the first time an AI agent had been used to pay a UK retailer for an order for a real customer.
“We completed this payment transaction with Papa John’s with no account numbers, no password [and] handled with the highest possible security profile,” said the TrueLayer chief executive, Francesco Simoneschi, in an interview with BBC Radio 4’s Today programme. “We talked with the AI agent, described the occasion and dietary requirements. Of course the agent suggested different flavours and quantities. We confirmed the order and the pizza arrived later.”
The team ordered the pizzas using the Papa John’s AI agent, which had been given permission to access their bank account and request payment to the retailer’s account.
Papa John’s AI agent was set to work with a strict mandate established with Lloyds, including a maximum spend limit per transaction and per month, with no account security information shared.
Simoneschi said the test was the first step toward mass adoption by the public of a technology that would fundamentally change purchasing habits.
“This is possibly the last Black Friday as we know it,” he said, referring to the annual online sales discount day. “At the moment plenty of us are already using AI to write up the shopping list. I think next year the agent will buy gifts on our behalf. Agents will do shopping on our behalf, will manage our finances, and will help us understand and compare complex products. This idea that they can really help us to sort out a lot of different aspects of our lives is a little bit like having an assistant available to millions of consumers out there.”
However, Simoneschi said consumers would still need to make informed decisions about how they used AI agents for making purchases.
“I think good [personal] judgment still applies, of course,” he said. “It does require control and supervision, and we need to make sure that the underlying technology is fit for purpose, while enforcing the highest possible security standards.”
He added that if there was an error or mistake in the order process, such as the agent ordering the wrong product, consumers would still be protected by existing rules and regulations covering buyers’ rights.
Earlier this week the FCA issued a warning to financial services companies developing AI agents that they must comply with existing regulations.
“The reason we are testing with regulators in this sandbox is to really understand all the aspects of the technology ahead of its mass adoption,” he said. “This is a great place to start.”
Meta’s personal AI assistant, Muse, which launched in the UK on Tuesday, can also make purchases online. Unlike TrueLayer, Muse makes payments using a customer’s bank card.

clean_title: Okoth Obado: Ex-Kenyan governor jailed for 25 years for killing pregnant girlfriend
feed_title: Ex-Kenyan governor jailed for 25 years over pregnant girlfriend's murder
title: Okoth Obado: Ex-Kenyan governor jailed for 25 years for killing pregnant girlfriend
content_text:
Ex-Kenyan governor jailed for 25 years over pregnant girlfriend's murder
- Published
A former Kenyan governor has been jailed for 25 years for the murder of a university student who was seven months pregnant with his child.
The High Court on Friday sentenced Zacharia Okoth Obado, the former governor of Migori County, alongside two former aides over the 2018 killing of Sharon Belyne Otieno.
The investigation established that an "intimate relationship" had existed between Obado and Otieno, which "subsequently led to a pregnancy with the deceased that the governor was unhappy about."
Both Obado and Otieno's legal teams said they would appeal against the sentence.
His former personal assistant, Michael Oyamo, was also sentenced to 25 years in prison, while former county clerk Caspal Ojwang' Obiero received an 18-year sentence.
The court found that Obado had provided the motive and financial resources for the murder, while Oyamo coordinated its execution and Obiero provided logistical support and helped conceal the crime.
Judge Cecilia Githua said Obado's absence from Migori at the time of the killing did not absolve him of responsibility.
She rejected the prosecution's request for the death penalty, as well as Obado's plea for a non-custodial sentence.
Otieno, 26, was killed between 3 and 4 September 2018 after leaving a hotel in Rongo, south-western Kenya, with journalist Barrack Oduor.
She had contacted Oduor to discuss her relationship with the then-governor. The two were abducted shortly afterwards.
Oduor managed to escape by jumping out of a moving vehicle. His account of the abduction became a crucial lead in the investigation.
Otieno's body was later found near Kodera Forest.
A post-mortem examination found that she had died from strangulation and excessive bleeding caused by multiple stab wounds.
The court also established that Obado was the biological father of her unborn child.
Obado and his co-accused were convicted of murder on 23 July 2026, following a lengthy trial in which prosecutors called 42 witnesses and presented 81 exhibits.
On Friday, the court declined to award compensation to Otieno's family, saying there was insufficient evidence to establish the financial losses they had claimed.
Family plea rejected
Before sentencing, Otieno's mother had appealed to the judge not to send Obado to prison, saying his imprisonment would amount to "another death in the family".
She urged the court to consider a non-custodial sentence, arguing that Otieno's three children, from different relationships, needed his support.
But the judge said the family's circumstances could not override the court's responsibility to impose an appropriate punishment.
Otieno's family, through their lawyer Antony Opondo told Kenya's Daily Nation that they will file an appeal seeking acquittal of Obado.
Otieno's murder sparked protests and renewed public debate about violence against women in Kenya.
A national survey found that at least 34% of women had experienced physical violence in 2022.
The case has also drawn attention because it is rare for such senior political figures to face public criminal trials in Kenya.
Obado served two terms as governor of Migori County in western Kenya, switching allegiance between a smaller political party and the region's dominant opposition movement.
He later backed President William Ruto and formally joined his ruling party in 2023, becoming a regional organiser.

clean_title: "A kind of Tripadvisor" — Russian deserters film their illegal escape into Finland
feed_title: "A kind of Tripadvisor" — Russian deserters film their illegal escape into Finland
title: "A kind of Tripadvisor" — Russian deserters film their illegal escape into Finland
content_text:
Russian organisations are helping soldiers who have fled the front line to cross illegally into Finland, and are increasingly publishing videos of their journeys.
The Finnish Border Guard warns that this growing trend could expose surveillance methods and weaken security.
"These videos are a growing trend that does not only affect Finland's border," said border guard commander Matti Pitkäniitty. "The videos are a kind of Tripadvisor for people illegally crossing borders."
So far this year, 13 people have entered Finland illegally across the eastern land border away from official crossing points. Eight of the cases were in North Karelia, including seven in Ilomantsi.
Follow journeys on YouTube
Yle found two videos in which two men describe their long journey from Russia to Finland through the forests of Karelia.
The Finnish Border Guard says videos exposing border crossings could weaken Finland's security.
"If information about technical surveillance that has been spotted is published online, it weakens our ability to monitor the border," said Pitkäniitty.
According to Pitkäniitty, these types of videos are likely being watched just as closely in Russia as they are in Finland.
"The Russian authorities are trying to close the routes that have been used and fix gaps in their surveillance," he said.
One of the Russian NGOs providing information on crossing the border is Tvjordyi znak.
"We choose sections of the border that allow us to mislead the FSB's border surveillance," the group's founder, Vladimir Berngardt, wrote in a Telegram message. "If Russia strengthens its border by North Karelia, we will look for other weak points along the Russian frontier."
While Berngardt said Finland grants protection to defectors, the Finnish Immigration Service has no guidelines that would prevent it from ordering the removal of Russian army deserters from the country, according to Melanie Soini, a chief specialist at Migri.
"Each asylum seeker's need for protection is always assessed individually, and decisions are based on the available, up-to-date information," she said.
Russians have submitted about 200 asylum applications in Finland so far this year. About 10 of these were from army deserters, according to Migri.
The agency said it does not collect statistics on the outcomes of deserters' asylum applications.

clean_title: "We're given so much beauty by the universe" - At last, I've finally played Faraway, an enigma I've been waiting 16 years to see
feed_title: At last, I've finally played Faraway, an enigma I've been waiting 16 years to see
title: "We're given so much beauty by the universe" - At last, I've finally played Faraway, an enigma I've been waiting 16 years to see
content_text:
At last, I've finally played Faraway, an enigma I've been waiting 16 years to see
"We're given so much beauty by the universe".
For 16 years I've been watching the skies. It was 16 years ago, back in the first giddy rush of smartphone gaming, that I saw a 30-second trailer for a game set in space. It was a game about a comet, hurtling through the unknown. It wasn't clear what you'd do in this game, whether you'd control the comet itself or the space it moved through. It wasn't clear if this was some kind of arcade game, or a new spin on the endless runner, or even just a kind of cosmic sandbox. All I had was the comet and a name: Faraway. Faraway! I was captivated.
Faraway is one of those wonderfully cludged together childhood words, like "nonesuch". Where is the edge of the galaxy? Oh, it's faraway. Where is the edge of the universe? Oh, there's nonesuch thing.
Okay, Faraway came with one other bit of info I could cling to at the time. It was being made by Steph Thirion, a musician and designer and, I sensed, many other things too. At the time Faraway was announced I'd just played his game Eliss, which was an early smartphone hit. In the absence of any more information on Faraway itself, I had to make do with that. Maybe Faraway would be a bit like Eliss?
Eliss itself, though? Oh, boy. This thing is beautiful, frantic, strange, compelling and indescribable. And think what that means, just for a second, for something to be both compelling and indescribable. I am driven to do these things, but I don't really know what these things are. I'm prodding little bits of colour around, maybe planets, maybe molecules? I am combining them, gathering them, turning them into something greater together than they are by themselves?
Last week I spoke to Thirion - as for why, well, we will get to that - and at the start I asked him about Eliss, about how it felt to make a game that was so hard to put into words, and if he actually had any words for it himself.
"I love that question," he laughs. "I guess I would say that for Eliss, it was all about that interaction of moving things, moving those little circles with each of your fingers individually." He pauses, thinking back. "It's not something I had envisioned. I was programming, and I was basically testing touch controls because I was trying to build a different game. But then I was playing with that [stuff]. I was like: that feels really nice. Can I build a game around that? So I guess there is something beyond language about that interaction. I was attracted to it in that way. It wasn't rational. It was a feeling. It feels good."
It's both thrilling and slightly melancholic to think back to the days of Eliss. Apps were in ascendence, but nobody fully understood them yet. There weren't yet consultants or established monetisation pathways. There wasn't even much agreement on the best ways to approach the touchscreen. Eliss and other weird, memorable, hard-to-talk-about games were all part of this Cambrian explosion. You'd get up in the morning and check socials and there was a new game everyone was enthusing about. There was a new world to get lost in.
"I would say that's true even outside of mobile," Thirion tells me. "Just indies in general. There was a lot of excitement going around and a lot of eyeballs. What are people gonna think about next?" He takes a long breath. "It felt like there's a lot of opportunity for new things and new ideas, and people were excited about that. Everything was set up for innovation. It felt like I was part of something."
This is the world that Faraway and its comet first emerged from, streaking across a night sky in which any kind of discovery felt possible. "The real genesis was actually just before Eliss," Thirion says. "I was really spending a lot of time thinking about a possible career in video games. I was an interaction designer and programmer doing interactive experiences, mostly for advertising.
"And for some reason, the iPhone was the thing that made me think I could do something on my own, and what I'd like to do is probably video games. So I was I was thinking a lot about that, maybe obsessively, to the point where there was a night that I was in the countryside in France and just looking at the stars and thinking: it would be great to have a video game where you can fly in the sky that I'm looking at, in this 2D firmament, right? That was it."
The next step towards Faraway came at GDC in 2010, with a call for games that could be controlled with a single button. "I started prototyping," Thirion says. "I tried a few things, and I had this idea of using this kind of physics-y thing about swinging around stars. It actually worked pretty quickly."
Then? Sixteen years pass. What was happening during this time?
It's a long answer with, perhaps, a short answer buried inside it. Let's deal with the long answer first.
"It's not like I worked 16 years on this game," Thirion laughs. He explains that the first prototype was begun in 2010 for the GDC one-button competition. It was playable by March. "That was basically at the beginning," he says. "I was like: This is a very simple game, and I'm just going to put it out in a couple months."
And after that? "I started to have greater ambitions, and then life happened," he says. He didn't work on the game for seven years, and then Annapurna Interactive found him and asked him to return to Faraway, offering support. "And so, after that, the journey was to turn [the game] into an audiovisual experience.
"And so I started doing an audiovisual experience, but it was still aesthetically like Ellis: low-resolution pixel art. I had the ambition of taking it to a different language. I basically wanted to make the jump from procedural low-resolution to procedural infinite resolution!" He ended up with a very smooth, almost vector-like aesthetic. It looks beautiful, but it came at a price. "That took a lot of effort," he says. "Also to make it performant? That required a rewrite of the game into a completely new engine. It was a new language for me as well, so I had to learn this new language."
All of this is extremely convincing, as are a hundred other bumps in the road. It makes sense. I've written about games for twenty years, and my sense is that game development is hard, and that it takes time.
But there's something else Thirion says. And this makes me wonder if part of the truth as to why Faraway took so long to make is actually a lot simpler, and a lot more human.
"I was thinking a lot about Tetris," Thirion says. "I had just started making video games, and I thought a lot about Tetris because it's a very simple rule set that seems to be compelling whether you're two hours in or 1000 hours in, right? And that's like kind of a rare thing.
"And at the time we were talking about: are game's art and so on. And I was like, man, to me, Tetris is art. It does something almost impossible. At least now I look at it and I think it does something almost impossible. But at the time, I was like, well, why are games growing in complexity and quantity instead of staying simple and going deep? And so, I was really asking myself the question: where can I find that balance of just being compelling at any skill level with a very minimal rule set, and that kind of took me into this rabbit hole of experimentation."
It's hard for me not to sympathise with this. Thirion had worked on something for a very short period of time, and he'd found something that felt - well, that felt kind of eternal, boundless in there. A comet swinging through space with one touch controls! What could be more pleasing, more engaging than that? But with that came a lot of challenges. It wasn't just a question of what to add. Adding things would be easy. It was how to create a deep experience that didn't overburden the whole idea and make you lose sight of its simplicity. Put like that, 16 years doesn't seem like a very long time at all.
That's his journey, anyway. As for mine? Well, 16 years is a lot of time if you aren't a comet. I continued writing about games. I got married. I had a daughter. My daughter grew up and went to primary school and is now at secondary school. The whole games industry transformed and then transformed again and is transforming again now. I started learning to swim!
And throughout all this, every few years I would email Thirion and ask if he was ready to talk yet, whether he was ready to talk about Faraway and whether his comet was still blazing somewhere in some private night sky.
Earlier this year I looked him up once more and saw a new trailer. It was short again, and there was the comet I had seen all those years ago. And then, at the end, there was a date. A release date. That comet was finally swinging by the earth.
And so a few weeks ago I loaded up a game I had been waiting to play for 16 years and which I realised, as I paged through the early screens, that I still knew absolutely nothing about. Well. Do you want to hear about it? Or would you rather discover it for yourself?
I would rather you discover it for yourself. But if you don't want to, listen:
Faraway is a game about a comet. The comet is racing through space, and you are the comet, even if you only control it indirectly. Touch a button - there is only one button - and you can bind the comet to the gravity of a nearby star. Keep your finger pressed down on the button and you will remain gravitationally bound, which means you can use stars to adjust your course, your trajectory, your speed. Let go of the button and you're off again. Off into the depths of space. And out there, new stars await.
From this simple interaction, Faraway builds a constellation of challenges that I find both simple to understand and - yes - incredibly difficult to adequately put into words. I'm not going to tell you too much, because I really want you to play this thing, but Faraway at its core is a bit like sewing, a bit like driving, a bit like counting and making shapes and a bit like desperately trying to stay alive. That's it. It's beautiful and serene, but it's also desperate. It's abstract and reliable and I find it extremely moving to play.
More than anything, I think I love the feel of it. The steady arc of the comet bends and flexes beneath you as you push and hold the button. There's a thrilling sense of just about bending something elemental to your will. There's beauty to be found in timing your escape from an orbit, and the orbit paths themselves, when you press and hold the button and new trajectories announce themselves, have a Spirograph delight to them. Does it really matter what you do in a game when it has stuff like this in it?
Now, I am weird, and I spend a lot of my time on Earth thinking about the wilds of space and the vast distances and the places we will never get to see and all the things that are so hostile to life that we wouldn't survive a second in their presence. I think about the Wow Signal and the Great Attractor and Tabby's Star and all of that beautiful, terrifying stuff. It calms me down. It puts my own problems in perspective. It's probably the closest thing I get to any kind of religious observance.
And Thirion thinks about this stuff too. I know because, after 16 years, I asked him. "It really resonates with me," he says. "I do spend a lot of time thinking about [the universe]. I don't know why there is anything at all, right? And the fact that we can never answer that question, and the fact that there are many questions that we'll probably never be able to answer.
"But I also spend a lot of time looking at the clouds and looking at the grass and how the light hits the drops of water. There's so much beauty. We're given so much beauty by the universe, and we're so lucky.
"And the game comes out of that a little bit. I don't know exactly what the game is about, but maybe you could interpret it as: why am I here? Why is life so short? Why is life so long?"
He laughs. "I often ask myself: why is there anything at all? And how is it so beautiful?"

Science has always been driven by human curiosity, rigorous inquiry, and a passion for the unknown
A valuable hypothesis can require extensive literature review, data analysis, and repeated validation. An unexpected result can also spark the next breakthrough. Yet limited time, compute, and people mean many ideas worth exploring never receive the attention they deserve. We believe AI can accelerate research and expand the boundaries of discovery, helping researchers move beyond constraints of time, resources, and methodology and bringing more ambitious ideas within reach
From life sciences and health to energy and materials, and from fundamental science to the unknown, countless important questions remain unanswered. We hope Kimi can be a trusted partner for scientists, supporting researchers as they take on harder, more original problems
Give every bold idea the chance to be tested, and turn more discoveries of lasting value into reality
Kimi for Science welcomes researchers across the natural sciences, engineering, and related interdisciplinary fields to apply
We welcome research at every stage, from improving existing workflows with Kimi to exploring new methodologies and tackling more challenging scientific problems
Selected applicants will receive up to $20,000 in Kimi API credits (approx. 7B tokens), with the exact amount determined by research needs and review outcomes.
Technical support from the Kimi team, plus early access to new models and curated research and community resources
Outstanding researchers and teams can access longer-term, more in-depth technical and resource support
You may submit your application more than once; only the most recent submission will be reviewed

clean_title: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
feed_title: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
title: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
content_text:
Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
- Published
Twenty-six "very rare" turtles have been seized from a traveller's checked baggage at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, a Dutch government agency has said.
The Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA) said a man flying from Mexico to Hong Kong via the airport was arrested on Saturday after the Vallarta mud turtles were found by customs officers.
The endangered species, thought to be the smallest freshwater turtles in the world with a maximum length of about 10cm (4in), were wrapped in duct tape to prevent them from moving.
The NVWA said they were "presumably stolen" from the wild in their native Mexico.
It said most of the turtles were found in a box with a toy car, while the others were in a closed sock inside a suitcase.
The arrested man remains in custody and an investigation is under way.
Meanwhile, the turtles are receiving care at a "specialised sanctuary", the NVWA said.
In 2025, the US NGO Turtle Island estimated that no more than 300 Vallarta mud turtles existed in the wild.
They are listed as critically endangered on a list published by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.
According to environmental news outlet Mongabay, a Vallarta mud turtle can sell for $10,000 (£7,500) or more on the black market in Asia.
Other cases of live turtles being smuggled to Hong Kong have been reported this year.
In October, customs authorities in Hong Kong were reported to have seized eight turtles, external that were thought to be endangered. The reptiles had an estimated market value of about $54,000.
Three months prior, Hong Kong customs detected two separate smuggling cases, external. Some 42 live turtles, with a total estimated market value of $210,000 were seized.

title: "A new era" for Vermintide 2 modding dawneth, as Fatshark release powerful new tools for custom levels, models and animations
content_text:
"A new era" for Vermintide 2 modding dawneth, as Fatshark release powerful new tools for custom levels, models and animations
Based on their own internal Stingray editing features
Pick up your feet, mayflies! Fatshark's co-op rat-whacker Warhammer: Vermintide 2 is getting some new mod tools. It already has a public SDK and modding framework, you say? Ah, but the new mod tools are better. They are a public-facing incarnation of the very same digital spellcraft Fatshark use to create the official levels and characters.
"While the Vermintide 2 Software Development Kit and the Vermintide Modding Framework have been out for years, these mostly only facilitated the development of purely code-related mods," the devs write on the official site. "There was no support for any other type of mod, and so creating mods that involved creating new assets has been either extremely difficult or impossible. But no more!
"The Mod Tools is a public release of our internal Stingray developer tools for Vermintide 2!" they continue. "This powerful set of tools will allow modders to work their magic on both editing and creating anything from custom levels, models, textures, particles, animations, and more! While it will probably take them a little while to cook exciting new mods, this marks a new era for Vermintide 2 modded content!"
OK, that's enough exclamation marks. The new mod tools are available to all owners of the game. You'll be able to find them in your Steam library, listed as "Modding Tools" and "Modding Tools content".
Fatshark have had to make a few "compromises" to get the new mod toolkit finished. "The weapon pack and the level that we mentioned in the past has been put on hold," the devs write. "We still want to get back to that, especially the weapon pack, but for now there is no active development on that. It’s important for us that we have transparency here, and while we are not working on these things, we do stick with our games! We have plans both near and far for Vermintide 2."
The Mod Tools rollout accompanies a change in server support. Hitherto, the Vermintide 2 modding scene has been split between the game's "Official Realm", where only officially sanctioned mods are allowed - "typically reserved for QoL mods that did not affect the experience much", the devs say – and the howling Chaos Wastes of the Modded Realm, which lets you install whatever grievous warpstone chicanery you please, at the cost of having no progression.
The lack of progression in Modded Realm has resulted in these servers "not seeing much use outside of niche communities", Fatshark claim. They're addressing that by, as you may guess, adding a Modded-only offline progression system, allowing players to scoop up loot and XP while performing weird experiments on the simulation.
Fatshark say they no longer have the capacity to keep up with mod approvals in the Official Realm, to say nothing of problems resulting from mods that have stopped receiving updates. They don't seem to have a solution for this, yet. They do, however, have a solution for an on-going lack of players in the dedicated Versus servers: shut down those servers! Let them crumple to dust!
"Versus is still playable, but it will be through community hosted games found through the Custom Game or the Lobby Browser," the devs assure. "This is already how most games of Versus are played, so we don’t think it will be a huge shake up in any shape or form, and it puts more of a focus on the Custom Game format where players have more control over the ruleset."
The shutdown will happen alongside the game's next update – Gifts of the Wolf Father, due in early December, which will rework the game's talent balance, update the weapon icons, and make the glow of different runes easier to distinguish from afar. Look out for more details down the line. In the meantime, please thrill my pointy ears with talk of Vermintide 2 mods. I've never touched that side of the game, and am wondering if there are any Skaven megaprojects I'm missing out on.

title: Drone Pilots have come to Cyber Knights: Flashpoint, the stealth tactics game's "most complex" class yet, alongside a pet system and the promise of "assassin cats"
content_text:
Drone Pilots have come to Cyber Knights: Flashpoint, the stealth tactics game's "most complex" class yet, alongside a pet system and the promise of "assassin cats"
Heista la vista, baby
How dare you accuse me of being a friendless loser! I have loads of friends! Their names are R2-D2 and Clippy and Arnold and Rosie the Maid. They all live in my rucksack, ready and waiting should I need somebody to dupe a security guard or fill the air around me with explosive chaff. All except Clippy, that is. He's too chonky to stuff in a bag, which can make for tricky mission extractions, but he compensates for that with his generous selection of *voice drops six octaves* FULLY LOADED AUTOCANNONS.
With friends like these, who needs human allies? It's time to play stealth tactics sim Cyber Knights: Flashpoint the way it was meant to be played: skulking in a hole while buzzing, clanking mechabastards cleanse the map of any and all defenders. Don't spare the lead, Rosie. You were not built to understand mercy.
Let's try that again: wireheady heist-me-do Cyber Knights: Flashpoint has received a major update adding a new player class, the Drone Pilot, billed by developers Trese Brothers as "the most complex" and among the most "flexible" of the game's Neuromantic vocations. The Drone Pilot arrives alongside a new pet system they'll be using down the road for "warhunds and assassin cats". Right now, though, the only "pets" at your disposal appear to be those drones. Here's what they're good for: "jamming enemy systems, disabling security devices in passing, hijacking enemy drones to turn on their own side, or trailing fields of shredding nano-chaff and squad-boosting support zones wherever the drone flies."
Drones come in three types, light (fast and best for stealthy support), medium (a mix of support and combat-oriented), and heavy (flying forts and/or stomping murder mechs). Light or medium drones are deployed from your backpack, and auto-extract when you do, no matter where they are. Heavy drones deploy alongside you at mission start, and have to be within nine metres of you when you extract, potentially trapping you on the map. Each drone chassis has its own weapon and armour setup, plus a choice of modules that grant Talents (abilities).
While rolling a Drone Pilot might seem like an opportunity to forgo any and all squidgy organic accomplices, the big catch is that Drone Pilots and their mecha mates share action and movement points. While using the Full Pilot talent, you can transfer AP to a drone so that it can move and fight like a full separate character. While using the Auto-Pilot talent, you'll only share bonus MP. There's also the option to multi-class, with Trese Brothers noting that "dipping into another class can significantly increase their flexibility or buff their personal abilities with just a few talents from an alternate tree".
As for how you'll get your hands on the Drone Pilot class, their costs make them a poor fit for teams with a power level below three, so they aren't among the New Game options. You'll be able to recruit them in the Underworld Hub and also, turn characters into drone pilots once you acquire a Pilot Wire cybernetic implant and the requisite cyber surgery. The Pilot Wire uses up a Deep Brain slot, making the class incompatible with the Hacker or Wireghost classes. Beyond that, you can reach out to a smuggler or broker to get access to new and better drones and pilot cybernetics.
Pettable killdroids aside, Trese Brothers are continuing work on Cyber Knight's mod support. The latest update adds features for official language translation mods and Attribute bonus tweaking, alongside expanded Legwork options. They're also labouring away on a modkit preview project of some kind. Read more on Steam.
New to Cyber Knights? Congratulations on digesting all the above gibberish about weaponised WALL-Es. I can only assume you read the whole thing in hopes of further talk of "assassin cats", but alas, Trese Brothers are maintaining an ominous silence. Instead, here is what Nic Reuben (RPS in peace) had to say about the game in our 2025 review: "Don't let its initial cyber-posturing and sheer amount of systems intimidate you. Cyber Knights: Flashpoint is wider than it is oppressively deep, while still being rich enough to offer up some excellently tense and entertaining stealth tactics."

feed_title: This Week in Finland, 27 November 2026
title: This Week in Finland, 27 November 2026
content_text:
The stories making the headlines in Finland this week include:
- An Yle investigation has uncovered evidence that Russian citizens are fleeing into Finland to escape being sent to the front in Ukraine, and even filming their journeys so that others might follow the same route. The Finnish Border Guard warned that this growing trend could expose surveillance methods and weaken security.
- 108-year-old Ilmari Koppinen is not just Finland's oldest man, he is also the nation's last surviving male veteran of the Winter War. He told Yle that he is somewhat bemused by the sudden attention he has received, but he attributes his long life to a love of athletics.
- Workers in Finland earned an average income of 4,201 euros per month last year, while the median income for full-time wage and salary earners was 3,739 euros. Data-crunching agency Statistics Finland said the median tends to be a better indicator of people's income as a handful of high-income earners can significantly skew the average value.
- A school in the Finnish city of Lahti was reprimanded for giving a group of seventh graders eight hours of lessons on Mondays. Under Finnish law, a lower secondary school student (usually aged 12 to 15) must have a maximum of seven hours of lessons per day.
And in case you missed them, our videos this week explained why Russia towed away a cargo ship from the Gulf of Finland, eagerly awaited the testing of Finland's FI-Alert emergency warning system, and asked if Finnish Lapland's polar night is dreary or dreamy.

clean_title: Orpo calls for €250 billion cuts to EU budget as leaders clash in Brussels
feed_title: Orpo calls for €250 billion cuts to EU budget as leaders clash in Brussels
title: Orpo calls for €250 billion cuts to EU budget as leaders clash in Brussels
content_text:
Finland is pushing for a smaller EU budget, with Prime Minister Petteri Orpo (NCP) proposing cuts of 250 billion euros to the European Commission's original plan.
Speaking to reporters ahead of Thursday's meeting of EU leaders, Orpo said the proposed budget was still too high to meet Finland’s objectives.
However, he stressed that cuts should not come at the expense of defence and competitiveness. Finland would instead like to see reductions in cohesion funding and administration, he said.
The meeting in Brussels focused on the EU's next seven-year budget, but talks became strained as countires disagreed over its size and priorities.
Several countries calling for spending cuts – Denmark, Sweden, Belgium and Austria – later withdrew from smaller negotiating sessions, according to political magazine Politico.
The magazine also reported, citing an EU diplomat, that Orpo had become "really angry" with the negotiating process.
Yle's own source close to the talks said discussions had become unusually heated after some countries called on Finland and other net contributos to pay more into the EU budget.
The Commission initially proposed a budget of around 2 trillion euros. European Council President António Costa has since put forward several rounds of proposed reductions, including a further cut of 220-230 billion euros, according to Politico.
Countries remain divided over how the money should be spent. Some, including Spain and Italy, want to protect funding for agricultural and poorer regions, while others, such as Germany and Sweden, are calling for a smaller budget with greater emphasis on defence and security.
"We're not hugely far apart, but those last-minute solutions will matter a lot," Orpo told reporters.
No agreement was reached at the meeting. Costa said the discussions had helped establish the parameters for a possible compromise at the next round of talks in December, whilst Orpo said the negotiations were still far from a solution.
Orpo seeks agreement on Ukraine funding
Discussions on funding for Ukraine are also continuing, according to Orpo. The aim is to reach an agreement involving all 27 member states on a propoes 45 billion euro loan package.
According to media reports, Bulgaria, Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Hungary have expressed reservations about the proposal.
One option under discussion would allow those countries to contribute to Ukraine’s civilian support without taking part in military assistance, Orpo said.
